issues.detail: The Greek 'προελθοντες' (having gone before/having proceeded) is a participle describing the state of the subjects. The Vietnamese 'đi trước' (going ahead/first) changes the meaning to a sequence or order of movement rather than the completed action of proceeding to the ship.

The Greek 'μελλοντες αναλαμβανειν' (expecting/intending to take/receive) is rendered as 'phải gặp' (must meet). The Greek implies an intention or expectation of 'taking' or 'receiving' him, whereas 'must meet' implies a necessity or obligation not present in the Greek.
